title: Plasmoids on the desktop should use KWin's Blur effect and settings
line: Desktop widget backgrounds now use the blur strength set for KWin's Blur effect, like panels and popups.
explanation: Desktop widgets aren't windows, so KWin can't blur behind them; the desktop containment blurs the wallpaper itself in QML with a fixed, maximum radius. Changing the Blur strength in System Settings therefore changed panels and popups but never desktop widgets. The containment's background helper now reads KWin's BlurStrength from kwinrc (watching the file, so changes apply live) and maps each of KWin's 15 strengths to the reach of its dual Kawase blur; the widget blur uses that radius, and the default strength 15 keeps today's look.

commits.message:
containmentlayoutmanager: follow KWin's blur strength on widgets

Desktop widgets aren't windows, so they blur the wallpaper on their own
and always used the strongest blur, whatever strength is set for KWin's
Blur effect. Read that strength from kwinrc and match the widget blur.

BUG: 512579

media.caption: KWin blur strength 1: the panel is barely blurred, the calendar widget still uses the strongest blur
KWin blur strength 1: the calendar widget's blur now matches the panel's light blur
Default blur strength, after: same look as before

review.text: Mapping KWin's BlurStrength to the existing MultiEffect radius is a reasonable approach since desktop widgets aren't windows, and the default keeps today's look. But it watches kwinrc with KDirWatch only because KWin's blur settings don't notify, which works around a missing notification in KWin instead of fixing it there; it also hardcodes a copy of KWin's internal strength table, which will silently drift if KWin changes it.
changes: In KWin, mark BlurStrength (src/plugins/blur/blur.kcfg) with notify="true" so the blur KCM writes it with KConfig::Notify
In plasma-workspace use KConfigWatcher on kwinrc [Effect-blur] instead of KDirWatch
Keep the strength-to-radius table but reference KWin's BlurEffect::initBlurStrengthValues in a comment as the source to keep in sync (or expose it from KWin if maintainers prefer)
